You use as + adjective/adverb + as to compare two things that are the same and not as + adjective/adverb + as to compare two things that are not the same.
We use as + adjective/adverb + as to make comparisons when the things we are talking about two things that are equal in some way.
For example: It is as precise as possible.
We use not as + adjective/adverb + as to make comparisons between things which aren't equal.

For example: Tindasia is not as financially balanced as the other islands in that area.

You use phrases in your writing to present evidence or proof and give background information.
Business e-mails vary by nature. They can be friendly, personal or neutral. The purpose is almost always to request and provide facts and evidence.
Phrases that you can use to present evidence and give background facts are:

I'd like to give you an update/report/summary.
It is precise/accurate/up-to-date.
As you already know ...
As you are already aware ...
The investigation indicates/shows/proves/reveals ...
To put things in context/into perspective ...
These phrases give validity to your writing and show your reader that you are presenting factual information and not simply opinions.
I'd like to give you an update on the situation.
It is as precise as possible while providing a comprehensive background.
As you are already aware, the rumour has been confirmed.
The investigation indicates that it employs 300 workers a day.
To put things in context: the situation is that the island of Tindasia is not as financially balanced as the other islands in that area.

Subject: Rumor Confirmed
Dear Janet,

This e-mail was not as easy to write as I thought it would be. As you know, we've recently been dealing with some malicious rumors about Holly's, and this situation, as it stands, is going to affect Polygon as well. I'd like to give you an update on the situation and it is as precise as possible while providing a comprehensive background.

As you are already aware, the rumor has been confirmed. It is a fact that Farmani outsources labor to the islands of Tindasia, and his factory is in the city of Shalopolis. The factory meets structure and workplace safety codes as strictly as it would in North America. The investigation indicates that it employs 300 workers a day, about half of whom are children as young as eight years old.

To put things in context, the situation is that the island of Tindasia is not as financially balanced as the other islands in that area. Basically, the poorest come to Shalopolis in the hope of temporary work. By sending their children to work, desperate families hope to survive. Farmani's factory is a legitimate workplace and people receive their promised wages. However, workers' rights are not as respected as one would expect. There are problems with their working conditions. Wages are low and no one has benefits or job security. People line up each morning and receive work on a first-come, first-served basis.
Up to now, Farmani has never visited the plant. He appears to have a hands-off approach, trusting various middlemen.

Regards,
Ferdinand.
